Topic 2 of 18

Setting Up DHIS2 Locally

Step by Step Guide: From an Empty Laptop to DHIS2 Running in Your Browser

Before You Start: Install Docker Desktop and Git

Install these two programs first. Accept the default options, and restart your computer if the installer asks you to.

Why Docker? DHIS2 needs Java, a web server and a PostgreSQL database to run. Docker runs all of these for you inside ready made containers, so you do not install or configure any of them yourself, and everyone in the hackathon gets exactly the same working setup.

Why Git? The setup files are kept on GitHub. Git copies them onto your laptop with one command, so everyone starts from the same files. On Windows, Git also gives you Git Bash, the window where you type the commands.

ProgramDownload it here
Docker Desktop (Windows and Mac)
https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/
Git Bash (Windows)
https://git-scm.com/download/win
Git (Mac)
https://git-scm.com/download/mac
Each step and what you should see

Follow the nine steps in order. Under each command is a picture of what your screen should look like when it has worked.

Step 1: Start Docker Desktop

What it does: Starts the engine that runs DHIS2 and its database.

What you should see: Docker Desktop open, with Engine running at the bottom left. The list of containers stays empty until Step 6.

  1. 1Engine running. Wait for this before typing any command.
Step 2: Open Git Bash

What it does: Opens the window where you type the commands.

What you should see: A black window with your name, the word MINGW64 and a $ sign, waiting for you to type.

Step 3: Get the setup files
git clone https://github.com/mohamedsillahkanu/dhis2-local-set-up.git

What it does: Copies the setup folder from GitHub onto your laptop.

What you should see: Lines ending in done. A new folder called dhis2-local-set-up now exists.

Step 4: Go into the folder
cd dhis2-local-set-up

What it does: Moves you inside the setup folder, where every other command must be run.

What you should see: The folder name appears after MINGW64. Typing ls lists the three files: README.md, dhis.conf and docker-compose.yml.

Step 5: Download DHIS2
docker compose pull

What it does: Downloads DHIS2 and the database software, about 1 GB. You only do this once.

What you should see: Two lines marked Pulled. The DHIS2 line takes the longest.

Step 6: Start DHIS2
docker compose up -d

What it does: Starts DHIS2 and its database in the background.

What you should see: Four lines with a tick. The database says Healthy and DHIS2 says Started.

Step 7: Check it is running
docker compose ps

What it does: Lists what is running.

What you should see: The database with (healthy), and DHIS2 with port 8010. Docker Desktop shows the same, with a green dot beside each.

  1. 1dhis2-local-set-up. The group holding both containers.
  2. 2dhis2_test. DHIS2 itself.
  3. 3dhis2_test_db. The database.
  4. 48010:8080. Click it to open DHIS2 in your browser.
Step 8: Wait until it is ready
docker compose logs -f dhis2

What it does: Shows DHIS2 starting up. The first start takes three to ten minutes.

What you should see: First Connected to database, then Server startup. Press Ctrl + C to stop watching; DHIS2 keeps running.

Step 9: Open DHIS2 and sign in
http://localhost:8010

What it does: Opens your own DHIS2 in the browser.

What you should see: The DHIS2 login page. Sign in with username admin and password district, then change the password.

  1. 1The address. http://localhost:8010
  2. 2Username. admin
  3. 3Password. district
  4. 4Log in. An empty DHIS2, ready for Topic 3.
